note: USACE Mississippi River (Pool 13) recreation area about 7 mi north of Clinton, reached by a mile of gravel road off Hwy 67. The camp area sits in trees west of a road that skirts a broad marsh; the open backwater channel lies beyond the marsh (not waterfront). Boat ramp, playground and picnic shelter. --Claude
summary: Facilities dump false -> true (rec.gov lists a dump station); sites 26 -> 23; season set May 15-Oct 15; FCFS scan-and-pay and 14-night limit confirmed; non-electric and $14 (2026-28) confirmed. Not waterfront confirmed. Pin fine. Note rewritten (old '3 mi N', 'no dump', counts and price were wrong or redundant).
flags: WATERFRONT: not waterfront confirmed. Imagery shows the sites under trees west of a gravel road that runs along the edge of a ~150 m wide emergent marsh; the open backwater channel (lily pads) is beyond the marsh. Road plus marsh between the sites and open water. Rec.gov's 'one of the best views of the Mississippi' and 'Directly in front of the campground is a field of lily pads' are marketing; no site photos are published, so no view is shown either. RIDB gives no per-site coordinates.

FIT: recreation.gov publishes no site lengths, and the RIDB catalog lists permitted equipment on only one of 24 records (that one allows RV, trailer, fifth wheel). Its own text says 14 or 17 RV sites (two paragraphs disagree). Nothing states a limit under 23 ft; no caveat proposed.
SITE COUNT: stored 26 (17 RV + 9 tent) came from one rec.gov paragraph; the same page says 23 sites twice and the catalog has Campsite 1-23. Written 23.

PIN: stored 41.93520,-90.18150 sits at the south end of the camp area near the entrance road (~170 m from the loops' centre around 41.9366,-90.1822); rec.gov's facility point 41.93513,-90.18422 is on the entrance road west of the railroad. No change proposed; the pads are under canopy and can't be located exactly.
